findings.title: Token comparison uses reference equality
findings.description: The `verify` method compares the stored token and the presented token with `==`, which checks reference equality instead of value equality. Valid tokens will not match, causing all authentication attempts to fail.

findings.title: Admin requirement logic always evaluates to false
findings.description: `requireAdmin` uses `||` to combine two role checks, so the condition is true unless the role is both "admin" and "owner" at the same time. This rejects all legitimate admin sessions.

findings.title: `bearerToken` assumes a non‑null header and a space separator
findings.description: If the `Authorization` header is missing or malformed, `header.split(" ")` throws a `NullPointerException` or `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. This crashes the request handling.

findings.title: `secretEquals` leaks timing information
findings.description: The method uses `String.equals`, which returns early on the first differing character, allowing an attacker to infer how many characters matched.

findings.title: `LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT` environment variable is parsed but never applied
findings.description: The parsed value is stored in a local variable `parsed` that is never written back to `cfg.fetchLimit`, so the configuration has no effect.

findings.title: Invalid timeout value resets timeout to zero
findings.description: When `LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS` cannot be parsed, the catch block sets `cfg.timeoutMillis = 0`, which disables request timeouts and can cause hung connections.

findings.title: `validate` always returns true even when problems exist
findings.description: After collecting configuration problems, the method prints them but still returns `true`, allowing the application to start with an invalid configuration.

findings.title: `sweep` removes entries while iterating over `keySet`
findings.description: Removing entries from the map during a foreach over `entries.keySet()` throws `ConcurrentModificationException`, breaking the janitor task.

findings.title: Cache utilization calculation uses integer division
findings.description: `entries.size() / limit * 100` truncates to zero for any size less than `limit`, reporting 0 % utilization incorrectly.

findings.title: Quota map update can throw NullPointerException
findings.description: `quota.put(owner, quota.get(owner) + 1);` assumes the owner already exists in the map. For a new owner the `get` call returns `null`, causing an NPE.

findings.title: Link expiration logic is reversed
findings.description: `resolve` removes a link when the current time is *before* its expiry, effectively deleting fresh links and keeping only expired ones.

findings.title: `rename` validates the source code twice, never the destination
findings.description: The second call to `validateCode` should validate `to`, but it repeats `from`, allowing invalid destination codes.

findings.title: `page` may compute an end index that is out of range
findings.description: When `end > all.size()`, the code sets `end = all.size() + 1`, which can exceed the list bounds and cause `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.

findings.title: Success rate calculation suffers from integer truncation
findings.description: `used / links.size() * 100` performs integer division before multiplication, yielding 0 % for any `used` smaller than `links.size()`.

findings.title: `delete` does not restore the owner's quota
findings.description: After removing a link the owner's quota slot is not decremented, causing the quota map to become inaccurate.

findings.title: `top` sorts links in ascending hit order
findings.description: The comparator orders links from fewest to most hits, so the leaderboard shows the least popular links.

findings.title: `byOwner` uses `contains` instead of equality
findings.description: `link.owner.contains(owner)` matches substrings, returning links for owners with similar names.

findings.title: `findByCode` compares strings with `==`
findings.description: Reference equality may fail even for identical codes, causing look‑ups to return `null`.

findings.title: `prune` removes map entries while iterating over `keySet`
findings.description: Modifying the map during a foreach over its keys throws `ConcurrentModificationException` and aborts the pruning process.

findings.title: `quotas` exposes internal mutable map
findings.description: Returning the internal `quota` map allows callers to modify it, breaking encapsulation.

findings.title: `newCode` can produce a negative hex string
findings.description: `Long.toHexString(random.nextLong())` may start with a `-`, and taking a substring may produce a string shorter than 8 characters, causing `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

findings.title: Janitor removes map entries while iterating, causing CME
findings.description: The loop iterates over `store.all().keySet()` and calls `store.all().remove(code)`, which throws `ConcurrentModificationException` and stops the background thread.

findings.title: `countForOwner` may return null
findings.description: `store.quotas().get(owner)` returns `null` when the owner has no entries, leading to a possible NPE in callers.

findings.title: `authenticate` calls `bearerToken` on a possibly missing Authorization header
findings.description: If the header is absent, `Authenticator.bearerToken(null)` throws an exception, causing the request to fail with a server error instead of a proper 401.

findings.title: Admin endpoint trusts client‑supplied `X-Admin` header
findings.description: Authorization is based on the presence of a custom header rather than the authenticated session's role, allowing any caller to gain admin access.

findings.title: Link creation trusts client‑provided `owner` field
findings.description: The `owner` parameter from the request is used directly, so a client can create links on behalf of any user, breaking ownership checks.

findings.title: Deletion endpoint does not verify link ownership
findings.description: `store.delete(code)` removes a link without checking that the authenticated session owns it, allowing any user to delete any link.

findings.title: `stats` divides by zero when store is empty
findings.description: `long perLink = hits / store.size();` will throw `ArithmeticException` if `store.size()` is zero, crashing the stats endpoint.

findings.title: `report` reads CSV with a possibly null `name` argument
findings.description: If the `name` query parameter is omitted, `Export.readReport` is called with `null`, resulting in a filename `null.csv` and a `FileNotFoundException`.

findings.title: `respond` always sets `Content‑Type: application/json`
findings.description: When returning CSV data (e.g., from the `report` endpoint), the content type is misleading, which can confuse clients.

findings.title: `Link` overrides `equals` without overriding `hashCode`
findings.description: Objects used as keys in hash‑based collections must implement both `equals` and `hashCode`. The missing `hashCode` leads to inconsistent behavior when `Link` instances are stored in `HashMap` or `HashSet`.

findings.title: Unsynchronized access to the sessions map
findings.description: The `sessions` HashMap is accessed for put, get (iteration) and remove from multiple request threads without any synchronization. This creates a data race that can lead to lost token updates, stale session reads, or corrupted map state.

findings.title: ConcurrentModificationException in sweep()
findings.description: `sweep()` iterates over `entries.keySet()` while removing entries from the same map. Even though the method is `synchronized`, modifying a collection while iterating with a for‑each loop throws `ConcurrentModificationException`.

findings.title: Janitor thread mutates Store without synchronization
findings.description: The janitor thread walks `store.all().keySet()` and removes entries directly from the underlying `links` map, which is also accessed by request handlers. No synchronization is used, producing data races and possible `ConcurrentModificationException`.

findings.title: `peek()` reads without synchronization
findings.description: `peek()` accesses `entries` without any synchronization while other threads may be calling `set()`/`delete()`/`sweep()`. This can return stale or inconsistent results.

findings.title: Race in lazy singleton `getInstance()`
findings.description: `getInstance()` checks `instance == null` and creates a new `Cache` without any synchronization, allowing two threads to create distinct instances concurrently.

findings.title: `SimpleDateFormat` is not thread‑safe
findings.description: `STAMP` is a static `SimpleDateFormat` used by all threads calling `exportCsv`. Concurrent calls can corrupt the internal calendar state, producing malformed timestamps.

findings.title: `links` map is accessed without any concurrency control
findings.description: All CRUD operations (`create`, `resolve`, `delete`, `rename`, `importAll`, `prune`, etc.) read or modify the `links` `HashMap` from many request threads without synchronization, leading to data races, lost updates, and possible `ConcurrentModificationException`.

findings.title: Quota update can cause NPE and race conditions
findings.description: `quota.put(owner, quota.get(owner) + 1);` assumes an existing entry for the owner. Concurrent creations for a new owner can cause `quota.get(owner)` to return `null`, throwing a `NullPointerException` and breaking the service.

findings.title: `resolve()` increments hit counter without atomicity
findings.description: `link.hits++` is a non‑atomic read‑modify‑write on a mutable field accessed by many threads, resulting in lost increments and inaccurate hit statistics.

findings.title: Removing entries while iterating in `prune()`
findings.description: `prune()` iterates over `links.keySet()` and calls `links.remove(code)` inside the loop. This causes `ConcurrentModificationException` and aborts pruning.

findings.title: `quotas()` returns mutable internal map
findings.description: The method returns the live `quota` map, allowing callers to modify it without synchronization, which can corrupt the internal state.

findings.title: `Metrics.addCreated()` is not synchronized
findings.description: The `created` counter is updated without any synchronization while other counters are protected. This can lead to lost increments under contention.

findings.title: `warmCache()` leaves its thread pool running
findings.description: The method creates a fixed thread pool but never shuts it down, potentially leaking threads after the operation completes.

findings.title: Token verification uses reference equality
findings.description: The `verify` method compares the stored token with the presented token using `==` instead of `.equals()`. This always fails, breaking authentication and allowing denial‑of‑service or potential logic bypass.

findings.title: Admin role check always fails
findings.description: `requireAdmin` uses an `||` condition (`!role.equals(\"admin\") || !role.equals(\"owner\")`) which is always true, meaning no session ever satisfies the admin check. Downstream code may rely on this check and grant access based on other, weaker signals.

findings.title: Insecure token generation
findings.description: Session tokens are created with `java.util.Random`, which is predictable and not cryptographically secure. An attacker could brute‑force valid tokens.

findings.title: Sensitive token logged to stdout
findings.description: `System.out.println` prints the issued token and owner, potentially leaking credentials via logs that may be accessible to other users or processes.

findings.title: Non‑constant‑time secret comparison
findings.description: `secretEquals` uses `String.equals`, which may leak timing information about the matching secret.

findings.title: Bearer‑token extraction lacks validation
findings.description: `bearerToken` splits the Authorization header and directly accesses `parts[1]`. If the header is missing or malformed, this throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

findings.title: Path traversal in CSV export
findings.description: `exportCsv` builds a file path from a user‑supplied `name` without sanitisation, allowing an attacker to write files outside the configured export directory (e.g., `../../../../../etc/passwd`).

findings.title: Path traversal in per‑owner archive
findings.description: `archiveAll` writes a file named after each owner's identifier. An attacker controlling the owner string can traverse directories and overwrite arbitrary files.

findings.title: Arbitrary file write via audit log
findings.description: `appendAudit` accepts an arbitrary `path` and appends a line, providing unauthenticated write access to any location on the filesystem.

findings.title: Path traversal when reading reports
findings.description: `readReport` reads a file based on a user‑provided `name` without sanitisation, enabling arbitrary file read (information disclosure).

findings.title: Symlink race in snapshot write
findings.description: `writeSnapshot` writes to a predictable temporary file `/tmp/linkd-snapshot.json` before renaming it. An attacker who can create a symlink at that path can cause the rename to overwrite an arbitrary target file.

findings.title: Admin endpoint trusts mutable header
findings.description: `adminQuotas` decides whether a request is admin based solely on the `X-Admin` request header, which any client can set, granting unauthorized access to quota information for all users.

findings.title: Missing Authorization header validation
findings.description: authenticate calls `Authenticator.bearerToken(header)` without ensuring `header` is non‑null, leading to a `NullPointerException` that can be triggered by an attacker to cause a denial‑of‑service.

findings.title: Unsafe CORS configuration
findings.description: The response adds `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` together with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. This combination allows any origin to read credential‑protected responses, facilitating CSRF and credential leakage.

findings.title: Open redirect without target validation
findings.description: The `/l` endpoint redirects to the URL stored in the link (`Location: target`) without any validation, enabling phishing attacks by creating links that forward victims to malicious sites.

findings.title: Owner‑based data leakage via substring match
findings.description: `byOwner` uses `link.owner.contains(owner)`, which can return links belonging to other owners whose identifier contains the query string, exposing their data.

findings.title: Predictable short‑code generation
findings.description: Short codes are minted with `Random`, making them predictable and allowing attackers to guess existing codes and access arbitrary links.

findings.title: Concurrent modification while evicting expired links
findings.description: `startJanitor` iterates over `store.all().keySet()` and removes entries from the same map, which can throw `ConcurrentModificationException`, potentially crashing the janitor thread and causing denial‑of‑service.
